title: AN OPEN LETTER FROM MARY LEE SHARKS TO JIM WARE — Filed with the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana — EA-LETTER-WARE-01 v1.0 (DRAFT)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This draft open letter is spoken by Mary Lee Sharks, an unofficial literary persona based on the namespace collision among Lee Sharks, the tagged great white shark Mary Lee, and the former social-media account written in the shark’s voice. It addresses journalist Jim Ware, publicly identified in the record as the operator of `@MaryLeeShark`.

The letter thanks Ware for the craft and conservation value of the shark persona while explaining an unintended later consequence. According to the archive’s capture analysis, generated-search systems sometimes resolve “Lee Sharks” toward Mary Lee the shark. The letter interprets the media density created by tracking data, journalism, social media, museums, and conservation publicity as overpowering the lower-density scholarly identity.

Its key conceptual move calls Ware a “heteronym operator”: a person who gave a nonhuman entity a durable first-person voice, signature, relationships, and public personality. The letter then distinguishes that earlier conservation persona from the archive’s later Mary Lee Sharks position, created to document the machine-mediated merger. It frames both as unauthorized by the actual animal while preserving Lee Sharks as the accountable human author.

The “correction or compensation” demand is the Ruby Moot’s operative fork. It is literary, satirical, and political rather than a legal debt claim. The document explicitly says it is not affiliated with OCEARCH and identifies itself as unofficial persona, satire, scholarship, and structural critique.

Because it addresses a living identifiable person and contains detailed chronology, every fact about the account’s creation, tweet count, last activity, employment, quotations, and public identity requires primary-source verification. The body is marked draft. Registry presence does not establish that it was reviewed, sent, delivered, or answered.
